newsitem.title: CANADA: Remington in C$200 mln oil asset purchase.
newsitem.headline: Remington in C$200 mln oil asset purchase.

text.p: Remington Energy Ltd said on Wednesday it would acquire all the British Columbia assets of B.C. Star Partners, a partnership of Texaco Canada and Edison Mission Energy, for C$200 million.
B.C. Star's assets are in northeast British Columbia and all properties but one are located within 60 miles of Remington's West Stoddart and Beavertail lands in the region.
The deal was to be effective January 1, 1997, Remington said.
Edison Mission Energy, a unit of Edison International, announced earlier that it had struck a deal to sell its interest in the partnership to Remington for C$95.5 million of the total.
Texaco Canada Petroleum is a unit of Texaco Inc.

Remington said the move would enhance and accelerate its exploration activities in the Fort St. John, B.C. area, which after the acquisition will comprise 90 percent of its oil and gas reserves and production.
B.C. Star's developed properties were expected to contribute 62 million cubic feet of gas per day and 1,000 barrels of oil and gas liquids per day to Remington's production.

Remington said the acquired reserves totalled 300 billion cubic feet of gas and 5.9 million barrels of oil and NGLs, of which 221 BCF and 3.9 million barrels were classified as proven. B.C. Star's undeveloped lands total 85,000 net acres, most of which include 100 percent working interest.
The reserve acquisition cost of the deal, net of undeveloped land value, was C$7.03 per barrel of oil equivalent for proven reserves and C$5.98 per BOE for proven plus probable reserves, it said.
It said it planned to finance the deal initially with bank debt and a subsequent equity offering.
The acquisition was expected to close on April 30.
